Four-Cycle Engine Theory Section 3: Four-Cycle Engine Theory Introduction Four events must occur in the correct sequence and at the correct time for the engine to run correctly. These events are (A) intake, (B) compression, (C) power, and (D) exhaust. (A) Intake (C) Power 001684 The piston is traveling from top dead center (TDC) to bottom dead center (BDC). The cam has opened the intake valve. The piston's downward movement in the cylinder creates a partial vacuum in the cylinder. Air at atmospheric pressure is drawn into the cylinder through the airbox and is mixed with fuel, supplied by the injector, as it enters the cylinder.The intake stroke is complete when the piston reaches BDC. (B) Compression 001686 Combustion is already in progress when the piston reaches TDC. The intake and exhaust valves remain closed as expanding gases of combustion force the piston downward. (D) Exhaust 001687 The exhaust stroke begins when the piston has reached BDC and has started its upward movement. The intake valve is closed, and the exhaust valve is open to let gases escape. 001685 As the piston reaches BDC, both the intake and exhaust valves are closed. The piston moves upward toward TDC and the fuel-air mixture is compressed. Ignition occurs just before the piston reaches TDC. G-Force V-Twin EFI Engine Service Manual 9

Systematic Inspection If engine will not start and the cause of malfunction is not readily apparent, perform a systematic inspection in the following order: 1. Fuel 2. Ignition 3. Compression This inspection, performed in a systematic manner, can usually be done in a matter of minutes. It is the quickest and surest method of determining the cause of failure. The basic inspection procedure is the same for all engine models. Any variation, by model, will be described under the subject heading. Checking Fuel Pressure Gasoline Units • (42 – 45 psi) For gasoline engines, check the following: • Is the fuel tank full? • Is the fuel stale? • Is the fuel pump working? Checking Fuel Pressure Gaseous Units • NG 3.5 – 7.0 in water column (0.87 – 1.74 kPa) • LP 10 – 12 in water column (2.49 – 2.99 kPa) For gaseous units, check the following: • Is there sufficient fuel supply from the meter? • Is the fuel supply pipe the correct size? • Are there any bends or kinks in the flexible supply line? Checking Ignition See Section 6: Ignition for testing procedures. Checking Compression Proceed as follows to check engine compression: 1. Disconnect the ECM. 2. Manually open the throttle plate on the ETC to wide open throttle (WOT) position. 3. Connect a remote button starter switch from the battery positive to the starter relay. 4. Remove both spark plugs and insert a compression gauge (Generac P/N GN04001) into either cylinder (one cylinder at a time). 5. Turn engine over with engine starter until there is no further increase in pressure. Record this reading. 6. Repeat procedure on other cylinder and record reading. The compression difference between both cylinders should not exceed 25%. More than 25% indicates loss of G-Force V-Twin EFI Engine Service Manual General Information compression in the cylinder with lower pressure. To calculate the difference in percentage, divide the difference in PSI (kPa) by the higher pressure reading. See examples below. Section 9: Lubrication System Lubrication System Description Generac GH-816 G-Force V-twins use a full pressure lubrication system with an oil filter. A gerotor oil pump draws oil from a screened oil pickup in the sump and pumps oil through the oil filter. Filtered oil flows through an oil gallery in the sump and is distributed to the main bearings, connecting rod bearings, hydraulic lash adjusters, and camshaft bearings. Engine oil pressure varies with oil viscosity, ambient air temperature differences, operating temperatures, and engine load. Oil Pressure - @ 70 °F (21 °C): 15 – 50 psi (103 – 345 kPa) NOTE: A pressure relief valve limits the maximum oil pressure in the system to 30 – 40 psi (206 – 276 kPa). Protection Systems Low Oil Pressure Switch See Figure 9-1. The engine is usually equipped with a normally open type, low oil pressure switch (A) which closes the circuit between the terminals when oil pressure drops below 10 +/- 3 psi (69 kPa). The engine will shut down on low oil pressure if one terminal is connected to the ignition ground wire and the other terminal is connected to ground. The low oil pressure switch can also be connected to an alarm or light to indicate low oil pressure, instead of shutting down the engine. A 009616 Figure 9-1. Low Oil Pressure Switch A delay built into the shutdown system on some engine applications allows oil pressure to build during starting. The delay allows the engine to run for about 10 seconds before sensing oil pressure. The engine shuts down if the engine is wired for low oil pressure shutdown and the system senses low oil pressure during operation. The engine will not run until 8 psi (55 kPa) of oil pressure is reached. If a restart is attempted within five seconds after shutdown, the engine may NOT start. The system needs 10 seconds to reset. Cylinder and Crankcase Cover Cylinder Finish (Cross Hatch) Recondition cylinder bores to restore cross hatch before installing new piston rings in a cylinder within specification. Avoid honing cylinder bores oversize. Oversize cylinder bores will permanently damage the crankcase. See Figure 10-4. Special honing stones are required when reconditioning a cylinder bore. Honing stones produce the correct cross hatch necessary for correct lubrication and ring seating. Honing is performed as a two step process called plateau honing. These steps must be followed carefully, and should be performed by a competent machine shop. The correct cross hatch angle is approximately 45º. 45º Figure 10-4. Cylinder Cross Hatch 004359 Honing is done with a variable speed 1/2 in portable drill and a honing fixture. Figure 10-6 at the end of this topic provides dimensions for making a honing fixture. Setup 1. See Figure 10-5. Use two crankcase cover mounting screws to fasten honing fixture (A) to crankcase. A Figure 10-5. Honing Cylinders 004360 2. Cut a wood block and place inside crankcase to prevent hone from extending further than 0.75 – 1.0 in (19 mm – 25 mm) below cylinder bore. 3. Clamp honing fixture and crankcase securely in a vise at a convenient work height. 4. Place hone in middle of cylinder bore. Tighten adjusting knob with fingers until stones fit snugly against cylinder wall. DO NOT FORCE. Place hone drive shaft in portable drill chuck and tighten. Verify cylinder and hone are centered and aligned with drill spindle. Honing Procedure Proceed as follows to hone the cylinder: 1. For the first pass, hone each cylinder with a 220 grit diamond metal-bond super-abrasive stone (such as a Sunnen® GMG55). Set drill speed at 240 rpm at 80 strokes per minute. Lubricate cylinder liberally to prevent buildup on honing stones. 2. For the second pass, hone each cylinder with an 800 grit diamond metal-bond super-abrasive stone (such as a Sunnen® RMG807) at 110 rpm drill speed at 80 strokes per minute. NOTE: Sunnen® lubricating oil (SCC605) is recommended. Automatic transmission fluid is also an acceptable honing oil. Another acceptable honing oil can be made by mixing four parts 30 weight oil with one part kerosene. Cleaning Proceed as follows to clean each cylinder and crankcase thoroughly after honing: 1. Wash cylinder and crankcase carefully in a commercial solvent or kerosene. 2. Thoroughly wash cylinder and crankcase using a stiff brush with soap and hot water. Rinse thoroughly with hot running water. 3. Repeat washing and rinsing until all traces of honing grit are gone. IMPORTANT NOTE: Honing grit is highly abrasive and will cause rapid wear to all internal components of the engine unless it is completely removed. 4. Use a clean white rag or paper towel and wipe the cylinder bore after cylinder and crankcase have been thoroughly cleaned. Any remaining honing grit will be visible as a gray residue. Wash and rinse entire cylinder and crankcase if any honing grip is evident, and inspect again. The cylinder has been correctly cleaned when there is no trace of honing grit on the rag. Apply clean engine oil to the cylinder bore to prevent rusting. 46 G-Force V-Twin EFI Engine Service Manual
